items.title: Implement entitlement storage, server-side resolution, trial anti-abuse and bring-your-own-key guards
items.outcome: Plans, features and entitlements are owned data resolved server-side with default deny, trials cannot be farmed, and the bring-your-own-key tier cannot be used to obtain features it does not include.
items.context: Entitlement enforcement is revenue-critical infrastructure rather than a feature: an ungated tier destroys the margin regardless of price. It also has to be the authoritative source, with any external provider treated as an event source only, so a vendor outage cannot grant or revoke access.
scope: Plan, feature, plan-feature, subscription and entitlement storage with seed data for every tier
Resolution middleware that denies by default and caches with explicit invalidation
External provider treated as an event source; stored state is authoritative
Trial limits keyed on a verified, hashed phone number with a database-level constraint
Refund-cycling counter feeding offer eligibility
Bring-your-own-key feature scoping and a server-side soft cap
Plan records created as immutable versions from the start, so T-BIL-10 pins rather than retrofits
acceptance_criteria: A tampered client obtains nothing; entitlement is decided server-side on every request
Absence of an entitlement denies rather than allows, proven by a negative test per gated feature
The trial constraint is enforced by the database, not only by application code
A provider outage does not change any user's entitlement
The bring-your-own-key tier cannot reach features excluded from it, proven by attempts on each
Entitlement changes write audit events with the old and new values
A plan is written as an immutable version record with a version identifier from the first migration; a mutable plan row is a review failure
Every subscription stores the plan version it was sold, so no later ticket has to reconstruct it
contracts_schema: Implements the published billing and entitlement contract including its explicit deny result
security_privacy: Phone numbers are stored hashed with a per-deployment salt, never in the clear
No provider secret is stored alongside entitlement data
observability: Publishes resolution rate, deny rate by feature and cache invalidation counts
tests: Negative entitlement test per gated feature
Trial constraint test at the database level
rollout_rollback: Shipped with every feature gate defaulting to the free tier so a bug denies rather than grants
Rollback returns all users to their stored entitlement, which is never recomputed from the provider
non_goals: Quota metering, which is a separate ticket
Provider integration, which are separate tickets
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns the entitlement schema, migrations and middleware. Clients read entitlements through the published contract and never cache them authoritatively.

items.title: Implement quota primitives: reservation, reconciliation and reset semantics
items.outcome: Quota is a server-owned primitive with reserve, commit and release operations, exact reconciliation for streamed consumption, documented reset semantics and an append-only usage record, consumed by the AI harness rather than implemented inside it.
items.context: The dependency loop between billing and the AI harness exists because neither owns metering. Publishing quota as a primitive here, against the frozen contract, lets both tracks proceed in parallel and stops streaming reconciliation being invented twice.
scope: Reserve, commit and release operations with a bounded reservation lifetime
Append-only usage event store with no in-place counter as the source of truth
Reconciliation for streamed consumption with headroom and a hard ceiling
Reset semantics with a defined time zone and idempotent execution
Short-window rate limiting independent of the periodic allowance
acceptance_criteria: An abandoned reservation expires and releases without consuming allowance
A failed reconciliation never consumes more than was reserved and never charges the user
Concurrent requests cannot both consume the last unit of allowance, proven by a race test
The reset job is idempotent under a double run and its semantics are documented and surfaced
Usage is reconstructible by replaying the event store
Exceeding the short-window limit returns a clear response including when it resets
At the published peak concurrency, sustained reserve, stream and reconcile traffic meets the latency budget and every quota counter remains exact
contracts_schema: Implements the published quota contract exactly so the harness can build against it before this lands
security_privacy: Quota state is server authoritative and no client-supplied counter is trusted
Usage events carry no prompt or response content
observability: Publishes reservation, commit, release, expiry and reconciliation mismatch counts
Publishes quota operation latency and saturation alongside reconciliation mismatch counts
tests: Concurrency race test on the last unit
Sustained concurrent quota load test with exact event-replay reconciliation
rollout_rollback: Shipped behind a flag with reservations disabled initially so consumption falls back to post-hoc recording in staging only
Rollback disables reservation but keeps recording, so no usage is lost
non_goals: AI-specific routing and cost control, which belong to E17
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns the quota module. The ai-service repository consumes it through the frozen contract and owns no counter of its own.

items.title: Integrate store billing and real-time notifications on Android
items.outcome: As a user, I can buy a subscription in the application and receive the entitlement quickly and reliably, and a purchase is never lost because the application closed at the wrong moment.
items.context: Store purchase is the primary payment path for the mobile audience. The failure mode that matters is a purchase that succeeds at the store and never becomes an entitlement, which produces an angry user and a refund rather than revenue.
scope: Purchase flow for the offered tiers with localised pricing
Purchase acknowledgement and consumption handled correctly for subscriptions
Server verification of every purchase; the client never grants an entitlement
Pending and deferred purchase states handled explicitly
Restore purchases and re-entitlement after reinstall
Clear messaging for grace, hold and cancellation states
Current plan, granting channel, quota usage, reset date, grace state and cancellation or restoration entry points
Upgrade actions rendered only when the server-provided channel-and-region policy capability permits them
Cancellation parity: cancelling is reachable in no more steps than subscribing, from the same surface
Auto-renewal disclosure at the point of purchase and before each renewal, with the amount, the date and the cancellation route
Dark-pattern prohibitions applied to the purchase and cancellation flows, checked rather than asserted
acceptance_criteria: A completed purchase results in the entitlement within the published time and the user sees confirmation
Killing the application mid-purchase still results in the entitlement once the server verification completes
The client never grants a feature locally on the basis of a purchase result
Reinstalling and restoring purchases re-establishes the entitlement without a support request
A pending purchase is shown as pending rather than as failed
Purchase screens are screen-reader traversable and usable at the largest text scale
Plan, quota, reset and lifecycle state shown on device match the server-authoritative values exactly
A channel-and-region fixture cannot render a prohibited checkout or redirect action
Cancelling a subscription takes no more steps and no more taps than subscribing, measured and asserted by a test rather than reviewed by eye
The cancellation route is reachable from the same surface as the subscribe route and is never hidden behind a support request
Auto-renewal is disclosed before purchase with the renewal amount, the renewal date and the cancellation route, and again before each renewal

No purchase or cancellation screen uses a pre-ticked consent, a confirm-shaming decline, a countdown that is not real, or a visual hierarchy that makes the decline action less discoverable than the accept action, each checked by a named test
A cancellation started is a cancellation completed: the flow never requires a second confirmation channel the user did not choose
Regional disclosure requirements are read from the versioned counsel-reviewed jurisdiction profile, and an absent or expired profile fails closed rather than shipping an unreviewed claim
contracts_schema: Consumes the published billing contract; purchase tokens are sent for server verification and never trusted locally
security_privacy: Purchase tokens are treated as credentials and are not logged
No price or amount reaches an analytics payload
observability: Purchase funnel events record step and outcome only
tests: Instrumented purchase, interruption and restore tests
Local grant attempt test proving the client cannot self-entitle
Plan and quota state reconciliation test
Step-parity test comparing subscribe and cancel paths
Auto-renewal disclosure presence tests at purchase and pre-renewal
Dark-pattern checks for pre-ticked consent, confirm-shaming, false urgency and decline-action prominence
Missing or expired jurisdiction profile fail-closed test
rollout_rollback: Released to an internal track first with real test purchases before public availability
Rollback hides the purchase entry point; existing entitlements are unaffected
non_goals: Web checkout, which is a separate ticket
Entitlement resolution, which is the api ticket

items.title: Implement web checkout for India and international payments with tax invoicing
items.outcome: Users can subscribe outside the store through a recurring mandate suited to India and an international card path, receive a compliant invoice, and never lose access because a renewal attempt failed once.
items.context: Card-based recurring payments fail frequently in the target market, so the mandate path is the practical route rather than a nice-to-have. Invoicing is a legal requirement for the domestic path, not a finance convenience.
scope: Recurring mandate setup suited to the domestic market, including its verification step
International card checkout for the non-domestic audience
Hosted payment pages only; no card data reaches our servers
Invoice generation and retrieval with the required tax fields
Renewal handling that grants a grace period rather than revoking immediately
Regional pricing applied consistently with the store path
Versioned jurisdictional invoice profile reviewed by tax counsel before a region is enabled
Tax profile per transaction: GSTIN capture and validation for business customers, place-of-supply determination, and the resulting tax treatment
E-invoicing threshold evaluation with the threshold value read from the jurisdiction profile rather than hardcoded
OIDAR treatment for cross-border digital supply, including the customer status determination it depends on
acceptance_criteria: A mandate can be set up, verified and used for a renewal, and the entitlement is granted on success
A failed renewal moves the subscription to grace rather than revoking access
No card data is ever received or stored by our systems, verified by a traffic review
An invoice is generated for every domestic charge and is retrievable by the user
Currency and price are consistent between the store path and the web path for the same user
Every payment state transition writes an audit event
Each enabled region names the required invoice fields and tax treatment in a reviewed, versioned profile rather than provider-specific application code
Checkout is blocked for a region whose invoice profile is missing, expired or unapproved
A business customer can supply a GSTIN, its format is validated, and the invoice reflects the resulting tax treatment
Place of supply is determined by a recorded rule with recorded evidence per transaction, so an invoice can be defended later
The e-invoicing threshold is read from the versioned counsel-reviewed jurisdiction profile; crossing it changes the invoicing path and the change is evidenced
Cross-border digital supply is treated according to the recorded OIDAR profile, including the business-or-consumer determination it depends on
Every tax rate, threshold and treatment rule comes from a versioned counsel-reviewed jurisdiction profile with a review date and an expiry; none is written inline
An absent or expired jurisdiction profile fails closed: the system refuses to issue an invoice asserting an unreviewed tax position rather than guessing one
contracts_schema: Implements the published billing contract; provider-specific fields never leak into the public contract
Jurisdictional invoice profile and invoice or credit-note schema with version, effective dates and review evidence
security_privacy: Provider secrets held in the secret store and never logged
Checkout redirects are validated against an allowlist to prevent open redirection
A GSTIN is business identity data: validated, stored under the same protection as other identifiers, and included in the erasure and export paths
observability: Publishes checkout starts, completions, failures and grace transitions without personal data
tests: Mandate setup and renewal tests against provider sandboxes
Negative test proving no card data path exists
Missing, expired and unapproved invoice-profile rejection tests
Provider-to-canonical invoice mapping tests per enabled region
GSTIN validation and invoice treatment test
E-invoicing threshold crossing test driven from the profile
OIDAR treatment test for a cross-border consumer and a cross-border business
Missing or expired jurisdiction profile fail-closed test
rollout_rollback: Enabled per region behind a flag; the domestic mandate path is enabled first
Rollback disables new checkouts while existing mandates continue to be honoured
non_goals: Store billing, which is the Android ticket
Payment provider selection, which is a commercial decision recorded elsewhere
Deriving a tax position: this ticket implements the position recorded in a counsel-reviewed profile and never invents one

items.title: Verify provider webhooks and make notification processing idempotent
items.outcome: Every provider notification is authenticated and freshness-checked before it is processed, and processing is idempotent on the provider event identifier so a replay is a no-op.
items.context: Webhook endpoints are the one place where an external party writes directly into the entitlement system, and they are unauthenticated by necessity. Verification and idempotency are the entry gate; the lifecycle state machine and reconciliation that sit behind it are a separate ticket.
scope: Signature verification and freshness checking on every provider notification
Idempotent processing keyed on the provider event identifier
Rate limiting and alerting on failed verification attempts
Rejected-attempt recording that carries no provider secret
acceptance_criteria: A forged notification is rejected and recorded as an attempt
A replayed notification is a no-op
A stale notification outside the freshness window is rejected
Repeated failed verification attempts are rate limited and alerted rather than only logged
A verified notification produces one normalized event carrying provider event id, effective time and pinned plan-version identity, and this adapter never mutates entitlement or quota state directly
contracts_schema: Implements the published notification envelope; the verification rules are stated in the contract rather than in the handler
security_privacy: Notification endpoints are unauthenticated by necessity and therefore rely entirely on signature and freshness checks
Failed verification attempts are rate limited and alerted rather than only logged
observability: Publishes notification counts by verification outcome and rate limit activations
tests: Normalized-event ownership test proving the webhook adapter cannot write entitlement or quota tables
rollout_rollback: Enabled per provider; a provider can be switched to reconciliation-only if its notification stream is unreliable
Rollback falls back to reconciliation-driven state, which is slower but never wrong
non_goals: The lifecycle state machine, reconciliation and the adversarial replay suite, which are their own ticket
Provider integration itself, which the checkout and store tickets own

items.title: Implement the subscription lifecycle, reconciliation and adversarial replay suite
items.outcome: The subscription lifecycle is an explicit tested state machine that converges regardless of delivery order, a nightly reconciliation detects drift against the provider, and an adversarial suite proves a forged or replayed notification cannot grant anything.
items.context: Out-of-order delivery is normal and a state machine that was never enumerated will eventually leave a paying user without access or a non-paying user with it. This sits behind the verification gate and is where entitlement correctness is actually decided.
scope: Order-independent convergence so late or duplicated events do not regress state
Enumerated lifecycle covering active, grace, dunning, expired, cancelled and downgraded
Downgrade that makes excess data read-only and never deletes financial history
Nightly reconciliation between provider state and stored state with a drift alarm
Adversarial replay and forgery suite running in continuous integration
acceptance_criteria: Events delivered out of order converge to the same final state as in-order delivery, proven by a permutation test
Every lifecycle transition is enumerated and tested, including the ones that lose access
A downgrade leaves all historical financial data readable, proven by a test
A deliberate drift between provider and stored state raises an alarm within one reconciliation cycle
The adversarial suite proves that no forged or replayed notification grants an entitlement
Each accepted transition resolves entitlement against the pinned T-BIL-10 plan version and reconciles quota exclusively through T-BIL-02 reserve, commit and release operations
An entitlement transition and its quota adjustment are committed atomically or through a replay-safe outbox, so a crash cannot leave split-brain state
contracts_schema: Implements the published lifecycle states; the state machine is generated from or verified against the contract
security_privacy: Reconciliation reads provider state with a scoped credential and never writes to the provider
Entitlement changes are recorded with their triggering event identifier
observability: Publishes transition counts, reconciliation drift findings and adversarial suite results
tests: Drift detection test with planted divergence
rollout_rollback: Reconciliation runs in report-only mode for one cycle before it is allowed to correct state
Rollback falls back to reconciliation-driven state, which is slower but never wrong
non_goals: Webhook verification and idempotency, which are their own ticket
Provider integration itself, which the checkout and store tickets own

items.title: Implement refund, chargeback and credit-note entitlement and quota unwind
items.outcome: A refund, a chargeback or a credit note correctly and idempotently unwinds the entitlement and any unused reserved quota it paid for, every unwind is audited against the charge it corrects, and a retried provider notification never unwinds twice.
items.context: T-BIL-04 issues invoices and T-BIL-06 owns the subscription lifecycle, but neither defines what a refund or a chargeback does to an entitlement or to quota that was already reserved. Left undefined, a refunded user keeps a paid feature indefinitely, or a retried webhook claws back quota a second time.
scope: Refund-triggered entitlement downgrade distinct from a voluntary cancellation
Chargeback handling that additionally applies the account standing policy a chargeback warrants
Credit-note issuance tied to the specific invoice it corrects
Idempotent unwind keyed on the provider event identifier so a retried notification is a no-op
Quota clawback limited to reserved-but-unused quota; consumed quota is never clawed back
Audit trail linking every refund, chargeback and credit note to its originating charge
acceptance_criteria: A refund downgrades entitlement within the published time and issues a matching credit note
A chargeback additionally applies the account standing policy, distinct from a voluntary refund
Replaying the same refund or chargeback notification is a no-op, proven by a test
Quota already consumed before the refund is never clawed back, proven by a test with quota partially consumed
Every unwind writes an audit event linking to the original charge
A credit note total reconciles exactly against the invoice it corrects
Every unwind resolves the subscription's pinned T-BIL-10 plan version and calls only T-BIL-02 quota primitives; no refund handler edits a counter or plan snapshot directly
contracts_schema: Implements the published billing contract's refund, chargeback and credit-note shapes
security_privacy: Refund and chargeback events carry only provider-assigned identifiers; no card data is ever received or stored
Credit notes are retrievable by the user but are not editable by any actor after issuance
observability: Publishes refund, chargeback and credit-note counts by outcome, and unwind idempotency hit rate
rollout_rollback: Enabled behind a flag once tested end to end against a provider sandbox
Rollback halts automatic downgrade and routes refunds to manual review; existing entitlements are unaffected
non_goals: Dispute representation with the payment provider, which is a support process rather than engineering scope
Store-initiated refunds, which the existing reconciliation job in T-BIL-06 already routes through the same lifecycle
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns the refund, chargeback and credit-note unwind module. It consumes the lifecycle state machine from T-BIL-06 rather than duplicating it.

items.title: Resolve cross-channel entitlement precedence for simultaneous Play and web subscriptions
items.outcome: A user with a simultaneous Play and web subscription, an upgrade, a downgrade or mid-cycle proration across channels resolves to exactly one entitlement, computed deterministically, and is never billed twice.
items.context: T-BIL-03 grants entitlement from the store channel and T-BIL-04 grants it from the web channel independently; neither defines what happens when both are active at once. Without an explicit precedence rule, a user who subscribes on both channels can be charged twice or see the two channels disagree about which plan is active.
scope: Deterministic precedence rule for when both channels show an active subscription, applied consistently regardless of which channel activated first
Duplicate-billing prevention that blocks starting a second paid subscription on the other channel while one is already active
Cross-channel upgrade and downgrade handling including mid-cycle proration
Single entitlement projection surfaced to every client regardless of which channel granted it
Daily reconciliation between the two channels' recorded state with a drift alarm
A versioned platform-policy matrix per distribution channel and region that tells clients which checkout, redirect and informational-price actions are currently permitted
Effective-dated service-fee and billing-fee records, including the announced India policy transition inside the roadmap horizon, with source URL, checked date and revalidation due date
acceptance_criteria: A user with both channels flagged active resolves to exactly one entitlement, proven by a test with both channels active
Attempting to start a second paid subscription on the other channel while one is active is blocked or redirected to a channel-switch flow
An upgrade or downgrade spanning channels prorates correctly and never double-charges
The precedence rule is deterministic and reproducible for the same inputs
Cross-channel state is reconciled at least once per day and a divergence raises an alarm within one cycle

The resolver returns policy capability flags from the reviewed channel-and-region matrix; a client cannot initiate a prohibited checkout or redirect, while informational pricing remains possible only where current policy permits it
Economics and pricing reports select the rate effective on the transaction date and fail closed on a missing or expired policy version; no fee is a source-code constant
contracts_schema: Implements the published billing contract's cross-channel entitlement projection
security_privacy: Channel identifiers are stored but never used as a basis for privilege beyond the resolved entitlement
Reconciliation reads each channel's state with a scoped credential and never writes to either provider
observability: Publishes cross-channel conflict counts, precedence resolution outcomes and reconciliation drift findings
tests: Cross-channel upgrade and downgrade proration tests
Channel-and-region policy matrix tests covering prohibited checkout, permitted informational pricing and policy-version expiry
Boundary test spanning the India fee-policy effective date and stale-source revalidation test
rollout_rollback: Enabled after both channel lifecycles, T-BIL-03 and T-BIL-06, are stable in production, behind a flag that falls back to store-channel precedence when disabled
Rollback keeps the last resolved entitlement rather than recomputing it from scratch
non_goals: The store and web checkout flows themselves, which their own tickets own
Refund and chargeback handling, which T-BIL-07 owns
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns the cross-channel precedence resolver and its reconciliation job. Android and web surfaces read the resolved entitlement only and never resolve precedence themselves.

items.title: Build the web customer billing portal with plan, quota and invoice management

items.context: Users need self-serve visibility into billing rather than a support ticket for every question, but store rules vary by region and change over time: some prohibit an off-store checkout or redirect while others permit informational pricing. This portal consumes versioned capability flags from T-BIL-08 and the refund and credit-note history from T-BIL-07 rather than encoding policy locally.

Quota usage display with its reset date, read from the published quota contract
Invoice and credit-note list with retrieval, reconciled against the billing history
Grace period, cancellation and restoration controls consistent with the server lifecycle state machine
Upgrade path driven by the versioned channel-and-region capability matrix, with checkout, redirect and informational-price actions rendered only when currently permitted
Plain-language explanation of cross-channel precedence shown when both channels are detected active

Quota usage and reset date shown match the server figures exactly
Invoices and credit notes are downloadable and reconcile exactly against the billing history
Cancellation and restoration reflect the same rules the server lifecycle state machine enforces
Keyboard-only and screen-reader users can complete every portal action, and the portal remains readable and operable at two hundred percent text zoom

items.title: Implement immutable plan versions, subscription pinning and grandfathering
items.outcome: A plan is an immutable version, every subscription pins the version it was sold, price and entitlement changes create a new version rather than editing a live one, and moving a subscriber to a new version requires recorded advance notice, so a user is never silently re-priced or silently re-entitled.
items.context: Every billing ticket treats a plan as a mutable row. Editing that row changes what an existing subscriber is paying for and what they are entitled to, retroactively and invisibly, which is both a consumer-protection problem and an accounting one: a refund or a dispute months later cannot be evaluated against a plan definition that has since changed. It is also the mechanism grandfathering needs, and grandfathering is the only humane way to raise a price.
scope: Immutable plan version records: price, currency, entitlement set, quota dimensions and effective window
Subscription pinning to a plan version, carried through renewals until an explicit migration
Version creation flow: a change to price or entitlement produces a new version and never edits a published one
Migration of a subscriber between versions with recorded advance notice, its channel, and the notice period
Grandfathering: a subscriber may remain on an older version indefinitely, and the conditions under which that ends are stated
Auditable history: which version applied on any past date for any subscription
Provider price mapping so a store-side price change cannot silently diverge from the pinned version
acceptance_criteria: A published plan version is immutable; an attempt to change its price or entitlement set is refused and the caller is directed to create a new version, proven by a test
Every subscription references a plan version, and a renewal preserves that reference unless an explicit migration occurred

Migrating a subscriber requires a recorded notice event with its channel and timestamp, and the migration cannot take effect before the published notice period elapses, proven by a test that attempts an early migration
For any subscription and any past date, the system reports which plan version applied, proven by a test over a subscription that has migrated at least once
Grandfathered subscribers keep their version through renewals with no action required, and a report lists how many subscribers are on each version
An entitlement check resolves against the pinned version, so a new version's entitlements never reach an unmigrated subscriber
A provider-side price that diverges from the pinned version raises a reconciliation failure rather than being accepted silently

Notice periods and any regionally mandated notice content are read from the versioned counsel-reviewed jurisdiction profile, and an absent or expired profile fails closed rather than sending an unreviewed notice
contracts_schema: Plan version identity and the pinned version reference are published in the billing contract, so clients render the plan the subscriber actually holds
Extends the entitlement resolution shape fixed by T-ADR-ENT-09 with the version that resolved it
security_privacy: Notice records are retained as billing evidence under the billing retention rule and are not deleted with a marketing preference
No plan version record contains personal data; it is referenced by subscription rather than embedding the subscriber
observability: Subscriber counts per plan version, pending migrations and notice-period breaches are all reported
A divergence between provider price and pinned version raises an alert
tests: Immutability refusal test on a published version
Early-migration refusal test and notice-period boundary test
Historical version resolution test across a migration
Entitlement resolution against the pinned version test
rollout_rollback: Existing plans are frozen as version one before any price or entitlement change is attempted, so no subscriber is migrated as a side effect of introducing versioning
Rollback is disabling version creation; pinning stays, because unpinning a subscription would reintroduce exactly the silent re-pricing this ticket removes
non_goals: Pricing decisions and packaging, which are product decisions
Store-side price configuration, which the provider console owns
Dark-pattern and cancellation-parity requirements, which T-BIL-03 owns
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Owns plan version records, pinning, migration and notice evidence. The web and Android billing surfaces render the pinned version; the admin console reads the version history and edits nothing.
